findings.title: REALM_ONLY cache searchKey includes organizationId unnecessarily
findings.body: In `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, the searchKey is computed as `organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""`. However, the underlying JPA implementation explicitly sets `ORGANIZATION_ID=null` in its search options for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` (and never consults the input `organizationId` in that branch), so the result is identical regardless of the supplied `organizationId`. By baking `organizationId` into the searchKey, callers that legitimately pass non-null values for `REALM_ONLY` (the Javadoc explicitly says `organizationId` is ignored when `mode` is `REALM_ONLY`) get a fresh, separate `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry every time, defeating the cache for any caller that does not happen to pass `null`. The searchKey should be fixed to a constant (e.g. always "") for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` so all REALM_ONLY lookups share one cache entry.

findings.title: Broken IDP cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin causes test pollution
findings.body: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` test, every `create` call is followed by `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`. The literal string `"alias"` is not an alias of any IDP created by this test (the aliases are `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19` and `idp-alias-20`), so when the cleanup runs, `get("alias")` returns `null` and `null::remove` throws a NullPointerException. None of the 21 IDPs created by this test are actually removed, so they leak into subsequent tests (and into the IDP alias cache of the test realm), which can break other organization cache tests. The same pattern is repeated in the new test on lines 381 and 425. The alias variable should be used (e.g. `idpRep.getAlias()` or a captured `final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i`).

findings.title: Broken IDP cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin causes test pollution (second occurrence)
findings.body: Same issue as the finding on line 381: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` uses the literal string `"alias"`, which does not match any IDP created by the test. The created `idp-alias-20` is never cleaned up, leaking into the realm's IDP store. The cleanup should reference the actual alias of the IDP just created.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without null check
findings.body: The newly added clause `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` assumes `idp.getConfig()` is never null. The `IdentityProviderModel` `config` field is mutable and can be set to `null`; `getConfig()` does not lazily initialize it in all versions, and callers using the SPI (e.g. test code, custom providers, internal `update()` flows that operate on partially populated models) may produce a model with a null `config` map, causing an NPE here. Because this predicate is invoked from `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`/`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` on every IDP `create`/`update`/`remove`, a single such model will crash the whole IDP write path. Either guard `getConfig()` against null (e.g. `idp.getConfig() != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`) or normalize the field in the model.
